svg.title: Hybrid quantization: two-stage re-scoring
svg.desc: Animated schematic of two-stage retrieval. 44 vectors are scored from small codes; the code's top 10 holds 6 of the 10 true neighbours. The code's top 30 are re-scored with exact f32 vectors, which lifts 9 true neighbours into the top 10; one, ranked 31 by the code, falls outside the shortlist and is missed.
svg.text: Hybrid quantization: scan with a small code, re-score a shortlist exactly
shortlist: the code's top 30 (f32 fetched for these only)
each dot is one stored vector, placed by its score against the query

g.text: missed: the code ranked it #31, outside the shortlist

svg.text: 1 · Scan. Every vector is scored from its 48-byte code, in memory.
2 · Cut at the code's top 10: it keeps 6 of the 10 true neighbours.
3 · Instead, shortlist the code's top 30 and fetch their f32 vectors.
4 · Re-score the shortlist exactly. True neighbours rise into the top 10.
Result: 9 of 10 true neighbours. A deeper shortlist catches the last one.
Schematic: 44 synthetic vectors. Measured over ten collections, re-scoring 50 f32 candidates recovers
0.95 (binary) to 0.99 (pq48) of the top 10, for 3–4% of the bytes an f32 scan reads.
